This tool remains the deterministic, caller-invoked path.

tools.description: Append a confidence-history entry; create the belief (gated) when the identity is new.

tools.description: Exact fetch by id (metadata + refs). A soft-deleted item is still returned, marked by two top-level booleans: `discarded` (operations removal) and `archived` (hygiene archive). A hub-distilled unit also carries a `freshness` key: its proof count, last reconciliation, stale state and reason, and the per-revision evidence trail (source ids and times only).
tools.name: get

tools.description: Return the authoritative structured snapshot only. It also carries two top-level booleans: `discarded` (operations removal) and `archived` (hygiene archive).
tools.name: get_snapshot

tools.description: Return the non-authoritative prose gist only. It also carries two top-level booleans: `discarded` (operations removal) and `archived` (hygiene archive).
tools.name: get_gist

tools.description: Regenerate the prose gist for one item (`scope` = item id) or every active item in the resolved bank (`scope` = "bank") from existing snapshots; snapshots are never altered. Archived and discarded items are reported as skipped, never summarized.
tools.name: summarize

tools.description: Report leaf queryability and dirty/refreshing ancestors, plus a `pressure` block: counts of dirty and refreshing ancestors, eligible hubs, pending and retry index jobs, stale distilled units with the source that answered and the last completed wave, and archive candidates. Each pressure entry is a count, or an unavailable reason when its source is absent or fails (no hub engine, failed hub eligibility scan, failed drain status read, failed stored-unit read, or failed archive scan). Archive candidates are an on-demand bounded scan — at most 256 items per band scan, two band scans — over the hygiene archive band (score 0.70 to below 0.90; discard-band items such as secret hits are never counted), and `incomplete` marks a partial scan. The `trigger` block carries the automatic maintenance trigger's last recorded decision for the bank: the evaluated pressure counts, whether the last evaluation fired a wave, the elapsed seconds since the last automatic wave and until the next one is eligible (the trigger keeps monotonic instants, so no wall-clock time is available for them), the waves in the last hour, and the last decline reason; a bank the trigger has not evaluated renders an explicit unavailable marker. The `index` pipeline block reuses the same one drain-status read; when that read fails, the `index` block renders an unavailable value and the call still succeeds.
tools.name: maintenance_status

tools.description: Return whether retrieval is needed for this turn.
tools.name: intent_gate

tools.description: Adaptive dense + lexical + optional graph retrieval. A hit may carry `entity_match`, a derived display-only inference that the query text mentions one of the hit's `entities[]` names under the documented containment rule; it is not a verification result, not a span-verified fact, and not a ranking signal. Each hit's `scores.age_factor` is the retention factor applied to `scores.final`: a pure number derived from timestamps and constants, in the bank's `[retention_floor, 1]` range (exactly `1` when the curve is off), and never null for a returned hit. Each hit's `scores.trust_factor` is the trust multiplier applied to `scores.final` at the shaping site: a finite number in `[the smallest configured trust ratio, 1.0]`, always present, that only reorders hits and never changes `category`, `epistemic_kind`, or `confidence`; it is not a confidence value. A hit may also carry `exact_render`, a bounded rendering of its authoritative half: it is content, it is absent unless the request asks for it, and it never substitutes for the `get_snapshot` read of the exact stored value.
tools.name: retrieve

tools.description: Return the bounded context pack under the token budget. Each included hit contributes one form: flow (default) is the narrative channel and must not be the only source of a numeric or identity-bearing claim, so read `get_snapshot` for the exact stored value; exact prefers each hit's bounded rendering, charged against this same budget_tokens. A hit with no rendering contributes its gist instead; a hit with neither a rendering nor a gist is marked as a reference rather than silently replaced by its identifier, and so is a hit whose rendering did not fit the remaining budget. The pack's per-form tally counts every form.
tools.name: compose_context

tools.description: Store process-local working notes; data is lost when the MCP process exits. Never durable or indexed (64 KB / 100-key caps).
tools.name: scratchpad_write

tools.description: Read one scratchpad key, or the whole session scratchpad when key is omitted.
tools.name: scratchpad_read

tools.description: Drop one scratchpad key, or purge the session scratchpad when key is omitted.

tools.description: Single-slot upsert: closes the prior value on both time axes and inserts the admitted revision.

tools.description: Read the currently active slot value, or a historical value at `as_of`.

tools.description: Store an admitted item in the cross-agent shared bank (bank forced to `shared`).

tools.name: shared_discard

tools.description: Reviewer loop: attest, update (auditable correction), invalidate, or discard a memory item.
tools.name: validate

tools.description: Read-only memory counts by bank, tier, category, age band, and provenance class. Two lists: `by_age_band` buckets active items by age in half-life units (the unit is the retention half-life in days, and each band's boundaries in days appear in its label), and `by_provenance_class` counts user_stated, agent_inferred, third_party, and fact. Pressure counts (flagged, stale summaries, archive candidates) appear when their sources answer, and a count that cannot be answered is left out rather than shown as zero. Tier is the semantic-versus-episodic split (semantic is category-scoped, episodic is the remainder) and nothing else.

tools.description: Read-only ranked noise scan: candidates by descending hygiene_noise_score with masked previews; never mutates memory.
tools.name: hygiene_audit

tools.description: Confirmed cleanup: flag | archive | discard (delete alias, non-compliance) | apply_suggested (apply each candidate's suggested_action; a keep suggestion is skipped). Without confirm=true: dry-run counts only, zero writes. Never performs compliance erasure or DEK destruction.
tools.name: hygiene_clean

tools.description: Masked durable hygiene-log rows (one row per item per clean action); every cleanup is reconstructible without secret leakage.
tools.name: hygiene_log_list

tools.description: Write one JSON memory_export_bundle with a completeness_manifest (version, counts, checksums, filter, complete flag). content_mode defaults to dsar_plaintext (authorized readable export); ciphertext_backup emits opaque bodies without DEKs. Requires a harness/system actor; no DEKs, API keys, or sync credentials in the file.
tools.name: export

tools.description: Write one content-free file of the ordered local event review rows (sequence, action id, state) under durable destination custody. Requires a harness/system actor; refuses to overwrite an existing destination.
tools.name: review_export

tools.description: Idempotent, manifest-validated JSON import of a prior export. Re-importing the same bundle skips everything (would_skip); force=true overwrites differing rows with an auditable reason. Every new long-term row passes the admission gates; dry_run reports counts without writing.
tools.name: import

tools.description: Provider importer: import memories from external memory providers (Mem0 supported; other providers return PROVIDER_IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED). Dry-run report precedes writes. Credentials are masked in all output.
tools.name: import_provider

tools.name: subject_request_start

tools.description: Report one stored request's state, technical completion, pending operator actions, and outcome as separate fields.
tools.name: subject_request_status

tools.description: Retry a confirmed erasure through its durable request id, then report the request. Requires a harness or system actor and confirm=true.
tools.name: subject_request_retry

tools.description: Record one copy-inventory disposition for a request and report it. Metadata only: no copy content, digest, key, or token.
tools.name: subject_request_copy

tools.description: Record a request-level retention exception and report the request; an approved exception yields a partial final outcome.
tools.name: subject_request_exception

tools.description: Read one content-free page of the local events bound to one request (sequence, action id, state) in ascending order.
tools.name: subject_request_events

tools.description: Record a verified Done result for one product-controlled path and report the request. Requires a harness or system actor in the request bank. Terminal requests cannot change.
tools.name: subject_request_path_complete

tools.description: Accept closure for one request, finalize its outcome, and report the request. A request with an open required action is refused.
tools.name: subject_request_close

tools.description: Report the derived peer state slots of one request from its durable per-peer rows.
tools.name: subject_request_peer_status

tools.description: Reconcile the pending erasure actions a restart left on one request and report the request; a settled peer action is proven by its durable evidence, never repeated.
tools.name: subject_request_peer_retry

tools.description: Record one peer disposition for a request and report the request and its peer states.
tools.name: subject_request_peer_disposition

tools.description: Read-only install/database health snapshot: backend reachability, schema version, banks, index coverage counts, and embedding readiness. Never mutates memory. A bound caller's `bank`, when it passes one, selects the bank inside its grant, and a caller without a credential gets the whole store whatever it passes.
tools.name: diagnose

tools.description: Deeper read-only consistency pass over referential integrity and index coverage; aggregate ok is false when any error-severity finding exists. A pass for a named bank is also not ok while another bank carries an error finding, and names those codes in notes; a bound caller's pass reads no other bank and so carries no such note.
tools.name: verify

tools.description: Compose an ordered repair plan from verify findings. Default dry_run=true prints the plan and registers nothing; dry_run=false registers the plan and returns its id without touching the store.
tools.name: doctor

tools.description: Apply allowlisted repairs from a doctor plan id or an explicit action list. confirm=true is required to mutate; unknown actions are refused and successful runs re-verify and report residual findings.
tools.name: repair

tools.description: Rebuild derived dense and/or lexical indexes. confirm=true is the live switch and starts the rebuild; dry_run is report-only, defaulting to the opposite of confirm, so a report-only run applies nothing and is not reported as ok. A live dense rebuild also needs an embedding sidecar.
tools.name: reindex

tools.description: Push local mutations for the given banks to the remote sync server since the durable push cursor; cursors advance only after durable accept. A bound call refuses a bank outside the credential's list or a `shared` bank the deployment has not enabled, and names the credential as `principal` in the response.
tools.name: sync_push

tools.description: Pull remote mutations and apply them idempotently (LWW + conflict journal); the pull cursor freezes at the last durable position when a mutation is dead-lettered. A bound call refuses a bank outside the credential's list or a `shared` bank the deployment has not enabled, and names the credential as `principal` in the response.
tools.name: sync_pull

tools.description: Masked local sync status: per-bank cursors, pending pushes, conflicts, open dead letters, endpoint, and auth/encryption state. Never returns tokens or DEK material. A bound call refuses a bank outside the credential's list or a `shared` bank the deployment has not enabled.
tools.name: sync_status

tools.description: Masked local sync-key report: the store as the literal `file` or `keystore`, a non-reversible fingerprint of 16 lowercase hex characters that two nodes can compare, the creation time when the store kept it and null when it did not, the key count, and a per-key list naming each key's fingerprint, creation time, whether it is the current key, and the store that holds it. Never returns the key or any prefix of it.
tools.name: sync_key_status

tools.description: Start the sync server on a background thread for the given banks; auto-stops after the TTL (default 30 minutes). Requires a harness or system (administrator) credential when a principal is present, and the scoped credential store passed as `token_file` (records added with `clio auth token add`); every served bank must be inside that credential's grant, so an out-of-grant bank is refused. `dev: true` serves without authentication, so it is an exercise/debug path, and a non-loopback bind is refused unless the operator setting `sync.allow_public_bind` is enabled. The operator setting `sync.max_envelope_skew_secs` bounds how far in the past an applied push's authenticated `transaction_time` may sit behind the applying node's clock. It defaults to `0`, and `0` disables the window: with no age bound a backlog a peer stored while offline still applies, which a store-and-forward log needs. An always-online fleet can set a positive value instead, and a push older than it is refused as stale, writes nothing, and lets the cursor advance past the row. A stamp far in the future is refused by a separate, larger allowance, so a fast peer clock cannot drop its data.
tools.name: sync_serve

tools.description: Operator ack-skip of one dead-lettered (permanently rejected) sync mutation so the pull cursor may advance past it. Without confirm=true: dry-run shape only. A bound call refuses an acknowledgement whose mutation bank is outside the credential's list or a `shared` bank the deployment has not enabled.
tools.name: sync_ack_skip

tools.description: Dry-run a batch of candidates under the bank profile: per-item decisions (each carrying `mission_rule_ids` when the retention mission fires) plus summary counts, writing nothing.
tools.name: admit_preview_batch

tools.description: Show the effective per-bank retention profile, its source, the optional retention mission (statement and example counts when set), and the fields stored but not yet honored.
tools.name: retention_profile_get

tools.description: Validate and store a per-bank retention profile; without confirm=true it previews the change and writes nothing.
tools.name: retention_profile_set

tools.description: Show the effective configuration after defaults, files, env, and runtime overlays; secrets are masked.
tools.name: config_get

tools.description: Validate and change a config value at session, profile, or deployment scope; secret values are echoed masked. A session-scoped value lives in this server process's memory for its lifetime and this tool does not write it anywhere. A profile-scoped value applies to the active profile for this server process, and this tool does not write it anywhere either. Deployment is the scope the persistence layer writes: the value goes into the deployment config file when one resolves. On the command line `clio config set` persists the `profile` and `deployment` scopes for later commands and refuses `session`, because a one-command process cannot observe a session-scoped value.
tools.name: config_set

tools.description: List named profiles and the active one.
tools.name: config_profiles

tools.description: Activate a profile in this server process's config session and return the effective-config diff; the change is visible to config views for this server process for its lifetime and this tool does not write it anywhere, while `clio config use` on the command line persists the same profile for later commands, and a successful apply pushes the profile's ranking environment into the already-open retrieval snapshot so the next retrieval uses it, while the admission policy and the intent gate stay on the ranking environment fixed at process open. Admission and category gates are never bypassed.
tools.name: config_profile_apply

tools.description: Show the effective hybrid ranking and admission environment for this process's config session: retrieval weights, admission weights, co-activation constants, intent-gate thresholds, the retention shaping group (`retention.half_life_days`, default 30, the age at which the decaying share of the floored age factor is halved), and the maintenance-trigger group (`maintenance_triggers`: `dirty_ancestor_threshold`, `eligible_hub_threshold`, and `stale_unit_threshold` each default 1 and trigger a wave when their count is greater than or equal to the threshold, with `0` disabling just that one condition; `cooldown_seconds` defaults 300 and at `0` means no cooldown; `max_waves_per_hour` defaults 12 and rejects `0`; `hub_budget_per_wave` defaults 16 and rejects `0`, because a zero budget would spend a wave and distil nothing).
tools.name: ranking_env_get

tools.description: Patch the ranking/admission environment for this server process's config session; the patch is readable back through `ranking_env_get` and `config_get` for this server process's lifetime and this tool does not write it anywhere, while `clio ranking set` on the command line persists the same environment for later commands, and the patch governs the next retrieval: a successful set pushes the new retrieval weights, retention half-life, trust ratios, and co-activation constants into the already-open retrieval snapshot and its association engine, so a `coactivation` patch reaches the association hub, the retriever's own query expansion, and the graph tools, while the admission policy, the intent gate, and the hygiene weights stay on the ranking environment fixed at process open. `dry_run=true` returns the normalized weights that would apply. Weights that must sum to 1.0 are renormalized or rejected with a clear error.
tools.name: ranking_env_set

allow_duplicate.description: Store this item even when its text is identical to an item already in this bank. Waives the exact-duplicate rejection only; every other gate still applies.

bank.description: Isolation key; overrides the connection default when present.

category.description: Semantic category; required for semantic writes.

context.description: Optional bounded descriptive source context, recording where the memory came from, such as a conversation type or workflow stage. It is not searchable: recall does not match on it, so put anything you want to find later in the item text or gist. At most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; rejected when empty or oversized, never truncated.

episodic_type.description: Episodic type tag; used instead of category for episodic writes.

evidence_ref.description: Provenance alias; copied into item source_ref when unset.

item.description: Candidate item shell (content lives in snapshot/gist).

id.description: Optional caller item id; generated when omitted.

snapshot.description: Authoritative structured snapshot (requires source_text when present). It is span-verified before commit, so on a verifying tool it may carry only the non-empty leaves entity, amount, and date; any other non-empty leaf is rejected. Put other content in gist.

subject_id.description: Data-subject id for DEK selection; defaults to the item id.

source_text.description: Span haystack for snapshot verification; required with a snapshot and rejected without one.

duplicate_tolerance_read.description: Read-time page similarity cap. Strict caps token-set Jaccard at 0.80, balanced at 0.90, lenient at 0.95; the neutral balanced default caps nothing unless a scope preset or prefer_consolidated is active.

duplicate_tolerance_write.description: Admission-time novelty cutoff. strict rejects token-set similarity >= 0.75; balanced and lenient add no extra cutoff.

maintenance_trigger.description: On/off switch for the maintenance trigger. On by default.

mission.description: Optional deterministic retention mission: keep/drop examples that steer admission scoring. Admission influence is arithmetic only; mission text is never passed to any model.

drop_examples.description: Patterns whose hits subtract 0.30 from the utility factor; reject=true entries (the default) reject outright with mission_drop:<rule_id>.

match.description: Match discriminator; literal is the case-insensitive substring default.

reject.description: Drop entries only: a hit rejects the write outright. Keep entries ignore this.

text.description: A literal substring, or a pinned-subset regex when match is regex.

keep_examples.description: Patterns whose hits add +0.15 to the utility factor; never rescues a gate or span-verification failure.

match.description: Match discriminator; literal is the case-insensitive substring default.

reject.description: Drop entries only: a hit rejects the write outright. Keep entries ignore this.

text.description: A literal substring, or a pinned-subset regex when match is regex.

mission_statement.description: Human-readable mission statement (what to keep, what to drop, and the tie-break).

pack_fidelity_default.description: Default pack fidelity channel: flow (the default) or exact.

provenance_floor_default.description: Optional floor on the provenance rung admitted when a caller sets none. Null means no floor; an unknown rung is refused.

recall_scope_default.description: Default recall scope honored by retrieve/compose when the call omits recall_scope. consolidated_only returns eligible consolidated units only.

retention_curve.description: Whether the retention curve shapes ranked results: each candidate's shaped score is multiplied by its age factor, never below retention_floor. On by default.

retention_floor.description: Lowest multiplier the retention curve may apply, in (0, 1]. Must be finite; 0 is refused, 1 is accepted.

theta_offsets.description: Bounded per-category delta added on top of the verbosity delta (abs(delta) <= 0.20).

verbosity.description: Admission strictness. selective raises theta by 0.08 and sets a 0.15 novelty floor; balanced is the unchanged default; permissive lowers theta by 0.08.
